text:
[LTAC.3.1] The compiler must rewrite each `after <dur>: <actions>`
clause into one synthetic timer fact assertion appended to the
parent rule's immediate action list, plus one synthetic follow-up
rule.

idris.name: ltac_3_1__body_runs_timed
idris.note: THE BODY RUNS WHEN THE FOLLOW-UP FIRES: the trigger pumped at 0 arms the timer; the advance to 6 and a pump fire the follow-up, which mints the `Delayed` and takes the timer -- temporal/LTAC.3.1.runtime's shape. Executed: working memory holds the trigger and the `Delayed`.

idris.name: ltac_3_1__lower
idris.note: THE LOWERING OF A RULE WITH ITS `after` CLAUSES: the parent with one timer emit per clause appended after its actions, then one follow-up per clause, in that order after the parent -- the compiler's terminal order, which the lowering gives the Idris model as rule ordinals. What the fixture lowering writes, on the model's rules. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_1__lower_tests
idris.note: THE TIMED TESTS the lowering gives with the rules: the parent's own, then each follow-up's guard. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_1__lower_untimed
idris.note: THE FRAME: a rule with no `after` clause lowers to itself, with its own test and nothing after it. A TRANSCRIPTION of the two definitions, said so: with it, Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's frame says every fixture the Idris model compared before this rung runs as it did.

idris.name: ltac_3_3__with_timer
idris.note: One synthetic timer fact assertion per clause, appended to the parent's immediate action list. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__one_shot_timed
idris.note: The lowered program runs as the clause's rewrite says: the timer armed by the parent, the follow-up fired at the delay. Executed.

idris.name: ltac_4_2__rules
idris.note: The lowering applied: the parent's timer emit and the follow-up rule. A fixture.

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__rules
idris.note: The lowering applied to the one-move fixture's rule. A fixture.
